projects.name: Horizontal Visibility Graphs for Heart Rate Variability
projects.summary: The idea was introduced as a research topic for presentation at Abhiprajna Competition 2025. A few recent developments on the topic were discovered and later taken up as a project to further explore the reliability of HVG as a model to measure and analyze chaos in HRV. The chaotic pattern of heart rate can be accurately modelled using time-series analysis of pulse data and analyzed using various preset parameters.

projects.name: Calculus of Variations and Differential Geometry Notes
projects.summary: Part of a study under Prof. K. Sandeep at TIFR-CAM, Bengaluru. This work was prepared using a combination of online and offline resources along with the professor’s lectures. I studied functional analytic techniques to rigorously define notions from multivariable calculus, including boundedness, continuity, Fréchet derivative, chain rule, mean value theorem, and the inverse and implicit function theorems. This framework was then used to study surfaces, patches, atlases, tangents, and normals from differential geometry. In the second part, these tools were applied to the calculus of variations, covering topics such as first variation, higher-order functionals, multiple independent variables, isoperimetric problems, inverse problems, and Lagrange multipliers. A particularly interesting aspect was revisiting the Fréchet derivative and the Dirichlet principle through variational methods. I am currently working on extending these ideas toward the study of Hamiltonians and Noether’s theorem from a purely mathematical perspective.
